extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, researchers, and practitioners interested in public apologies, reparations, restorative justice, and human rights
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and descriptive standards for what constitutes a public apology—its role in reparations and restorative justice, and the key components and practices that make an apology effective in public/institutional contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public apology as a component of reparation (UN OHCHR)
rubrics_metrics.description: A public apology is a component of reparation as stipulated in the United Nations Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights resolution proclaiming the Basic Principles and Guidelines on the Right to a Remedy and Reparation for Victims of Gross Violations of International Human Rights Law and Serious Violations of International Humanitarian Law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When used in the context of official reparations, a public apology functions as one element in a state or institution's obligation to provide remedy and reparation to victims; examples on the page (France, Canada) illustrate state-level apologies tied to historical injustices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public apology as a restorative process
rubrics_metrics.description: A public apology is defined as a restorative process intended to heal and to generate forgiveness on the part of the offended party, for the improper behavior or action of the offender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The goal is healing and forgiveness rather than merely rhetorical expression; effective apologies should be oriented toward repairing relational and social harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three core components of a public apology
rubrics_metrics.description: The process consists in three components: acknowledgment of wrongdoing, admission of responsibility and the action of the wrongdoer to compensate damages produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three elements are presented as necessary parts of the apology process—acknowledging what occurred, accepting responsibility, and taking tangible steps to compensate or remediate the harm. Examples (state apologies, corporate apologies) demonstrate application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of social interaction and moral commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Besides the role of healing and bringing forgiveness on the part of the offended party, public apologies have the function of restoring the health of the social interaction and 'publicly acknowledging a shared commitment to some moral values'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An effective public apology should signal recommitment to shared moral norms and help restore trust in social relationships or institutions; publicness and moral framing are emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements for restoring moral relations (Cohen 2016)
rubrics_metrics.description: According to Cohen (2016): 'In order to restore or create moral relations among transgressors and their victims, transgressors …. need to admit their wrongdoing, commemorate or memorialize history, and, most notably, provide an apology.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This frames apology as one element of a broader practice that includes admitting wrongdoing and commemorating/memorializing history—suggesting that remembrance and recognition of past harms accompany apologies to make them meaningful.
